condition.label: proximal hamstring tendinopathy
condition.distinctions: Focal chronic proximal hamstring tendon pain; distinguish lumbar/sciatic referral, acute rupture/avulsion and postoperative repair.

scope.operativeStatus: Nonoperative rehabilitation only; postoperative pathways require separate assessment.

scope.uncertainty: Source eligibility limits applicability; it does not establish contraindications.

protocol.execution: Supine hamstring bridge, double/single leg; modify support/load. Later modified deadlift/lunge with graded hip flexion.
protocol.dose: Isometric 5×30–45 s; 90 seconds rest. Compression 2×4–6→3×6–8, 2 minutes rest.
protocol.frequency: Isometric as-needed up to 4/day; compression 3/week/every second day.
protocol.progression: Quality 45-second holds; compression angle to sport/work demands.
protocol.stoppingRules: Stage 1 pain≤ 4/10 by second rep; reduce load if latent> 2/10 increase persists> 24 h.

gaps: All material is draft and clinically unreviewed; no runtime mapping, supported-condition claim, default dose or escalation clearance follows.
No universal numeric load/range cap or hard exercise contraindication was established; benefit from alternatives and trial exclusions do not prove harm.
Concurrent condition restrictions, equipment requirements and independent joint limits remain controlling; stretching never earns strength-set credit or generic five-second progression.
No untreated comparison or equivalence conclusion; isometric analgesia remains a rationale rather than proven isolated PHT effect.
No permanent ban on hip flexion, squatting, deadlifting or hamstring stretching follows; compression was deliberately reintroduced.
